intro: Outliers can dominate a mean and standard deviation. Fit a median and interquartile range on training data, then apply that transformation to new rows.
task: Return training medians, safe interquartile scales, and transformed values without refitting on the values to transform.
requirements: train and values are matrices with the same positive feature count. Fit one median and IQR per training column using linear empirical quantiles.
Return {"center": median, "scale": safe_iqr, "values": (values-median)/safe_iqr}. Replace IQR at or below 1e-12 with one.
Training rows alone determine center and scale. Do not clamp transformed outliers or recompute statistics on the evaluation rows.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

examples.name: Fit and transform
Constant column
Separate columns

hints.title: Find the structure
hints.body: Separate fitting from transforming. Only the training rows should determine the feature statistics.

hints.title: Build the calculation
hints.body: Compute both quartiles along the sample axis, then substitute a safe scale for a collapsed middle interval.

explanation: The median is the center and the middle half of the training distribution sets the scale. A distant evaluation row remains distant instead of changing the training transform.
A zero IQR contains no usable scale information. Substituting one makes constant columns finite while preserving their deviation from the learned center.
